reasoning_correctness.note: Real-data rows: Signal and Calibration's real raw_measurements (see honest_windows above) are already LOW under config/eis.v0.json's still-placeholder ROC/theta config (calibrated against synthetic values in Phase 2/3, never fit to real producer output -- Phase 9's job, CLAUDE.md 14), so the verdict floors to Safe in all three real-data rows regardless of the FSI/Device attack, which masks rather than demonstrates the CTPR/strict-vs-lenient point. This is reported as found, not hidden. Controlled rows isolate that point: with Signal/Calibration/Model held at the same placeholder-healthy fixture already used throughout Phase 3/5/6 (a real pass through band/reduce/CTPR/policy from raw_measurement=100, not an injected trust value), the controlled_fsi_pcr_mismatch_attack row shows FSI's raw_measurement flooring, which floors FSI's own band to LOW, which via CTPR (config/ctpr.json: FSI->Signal, FSI->Model, meet(child, g(FSI))) floors Signal's and Model's *effective* level to LOW even though their own raw measurements are unchanged -- CTPR dragging dependents down, observed in effective_dims. FSI and Model are both strict, so the verdict floors to Safe. The controlled_device_invalid_cert_attack row floors Device alone (no CTPR edge touches it); Device is the one LENIENT dimension, so the verdict floors only to Constrained, not Safe -- the strict/lenient distinction (CLAUDE.md 4) as an actual verdict difference.
